transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-21
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood CSM), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sara Mitchell (Lumina Head of ML), Brian Cole (Platform Eng), Anika Rao (Security), James O'Neill (PM)

Summary: Kickoff for Redwood onboarding and implementation planning. Covered roles, initial success criteria, security/compliance checklist (SOC2, KMS), VPC/private deployment options, sandbox/API access, and next steps for technical deep dive and weekly cadence. Some transcription noise on product names and acronyms.

Topics: onboarding timeline, sandbox setup, VPC & networking, SSO & SAML, data residency, test prompts & evals, pilot metrics, pricing/commits for dedicated capacity (brief)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we're excited to kick this off with Lumina. I think we have the right folks, uh, can we do quick round of intros?
[00:18] Sara Mitchell: Sure I'm Sara, Head of ML at Lumina. We're building a clinical notes enrichment pipeline, want to use Redwood for inference for summarization and entity extraction.
[00:28] Brian Cole: Brian, platform eng, i'll be responsible for networking and infra hooks, we'll own the VPC peering and onboarding.
[00:34] Anika Rao: Anika, security and compliance, i'll be asking SOC2, KMS, retention questions.
[00:40] James O'Neill: James, product, i'll be working with Sara on acceptance criteria and rollout plan.
[00:46] Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick from our side Ravi is going to be your CSM for a weekly check in cadence and Diego here is your SE who will run the technical deep dives.
[00:56] Ravi Patel: Hey all, happy to be here, we'll keep the onboarding timeline tight and make sure you get sandbox keys and access.
[01:05] Diego Alvarez: Hi, i'll focus on latency/cost tuning, batching, and the VPC/private deployment details.

[01:20] Maya Chen: High level agenda, we'll cover goals and success criteria, timeline, security and VPC options, sandbox and API onboarding, folks to follow up on next steps. Sound good?
[01:30] James O'Neill: Yep.

[01:38] Sara Mitchell: Our immediate timeline: pilot in 6 weeks, want to evaluate behaviour on 1M tokens/day with 100 qps bursts, and latency ideally under 200-300 ms per request. Those numbers are a bit aspirational, but that's what we want to test.
[01:58] Diego Alvarez: Okay that's helpful. We'll run some benchmarks in the sandbox and tune batching/kv cache. If you want 200-300ms for short context that usually means dedicated capacity or aggressive batching tradeoffs, we can discuss tradeoffs.
[02:12] Brian Cole: When you say sandbox, do we get VPC peering or is that hosted? We need to know network egress, we have strict firewall policies.
[02:20] Ravi Patel: Good call — initial sandbox will be hosted/shared with obfuscated data by default; we can do a private VPC sandbox if you prefer, Diego will outline steps.

[02:34] Diego Alvarez: Right, options are: hosted (fastest onboarding), dedicated with reserved capacity, or private VPC deployment (customer-managed network). For regulated PII stuff we usually recommend private or dedicated depending on volume.
[02:48] Anika Rao: For Lumina we need KMS integration and proof of key custody; also retention controls — can Redwood provide logs and an audit trail that we can ingest into our SIEM?
[02:58] Diego Alvarez: Yes we have audit logs and key management integrations (KMS/HSM). We'll share the security pack; it's linked in the deck, but i'll make sure to send the specific KMS integration doc.
[03:12] Maya Chen: We'll share SOC2 certificate and the security packet after the call.

[03:18] Sara Mitchell: Are there any baseline throughput guarantees for dedicated pools? We're expecting spikes when batch jobs run at night.
[03:26] Ravi Patel: Dedicated capacity comes with SLA-backed throughput, and you can configure autoscale and burst capacity. We'll include the SLA language in the docs.

[03:36] James O'Neill: On the evaluation we'll need a simple success criteria doc — like throughput, latency, and quality targets — can Redwood help draft that?
[03:44] Maya Chen: Yes we'll draft a pilot success criteria template and share it.

[03:50] [05:00] -- (brief side conversation about calendar times and timezone) --
[05:14] Diego Alvarez: Technical notes — for low-latency use cases we recommend enabling prefix KV caching and sequence-length aware batching; those reduce per-token cost and latency, but require some infra hooks.
[05:30] Brian Cole: Can you share a sample terraform or networking example for the VPC peering? Our security team wants to review it.
[05:38] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely, i'll send a sample terraform repo and a network diagram. I have a gist I'll attach: https://redwood.co/docs/vpc-terraform (note: may transcribe link slightly wrong in auto export)

[06:00] Anika Rao: For SSO we use Okta, need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning — is that supported?
[06:08] Ravi Patel: Yes Okta SAML and SCIM are supported. We'll send the SSO setup guide and the necessary metadata files.

[06:22] Sara Mitchell: Regarding data residency, some of our customers require EU residency, do you have region controls?
[06:28] Diego Alvarez: Yes we have region routing and can pin deployment to region or private deployment in EU. We'll capture region in the onboarding form.

[06:42] James O'Neill: Any immediate blockers we should be aware of?
[06:45] Brian Cole: We'll need a security review, and we'll want to test private sandbox networking. Also need to confirm cost model for peak bursts.
[06:55] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll add those to action items.

[07:02] [10:00] -- Customer asks about pricing and committed capacity briefly --
[10:18] Maya Chen: For pricing, hosted is usage-based per token/embedding, dedicated is reserved capacity monthly/annual. For the pilot we usually recommend hosted sandbox then move to dedicated if you want guaranteed throughput. We'll follow up with a short pricing summary.
[10:34] Sara Mitchell: Sounds good.

[10:42] Diego Alvarez: I want to flag one thing: when doing latency sensitive work, quantization strategy can affect accuracy. We'll help tune quantization settings per model during the pilot.
[10:56] Sara Mitchell: Perfect. We'll want to set a baseline eval set to track regressions.

[11:10] Ravi Patel: We'll also enable quality monitoring and alerts tied to prompt sets, and we can wire that into your Slack or PagerDuty for regressions.

[11:22] [15:00] -- Discussion of documentation and decks --
[15:15] Maya Chen: I'll attach the onboarding checklist, security pack, and pilot success template after the call.
[15:22] Anika Rao: Please include specifics about KMS integrations and data retention periods.

[15:30] Brian Cole: One thing on network egress costs — does Redwood charge for egress? we need to model costs for cloud egress on our side.
[15:38] Ravi Patel: We don't charge for customer cloud egress from Redwood; usual cloud provider egress still applies when hosting in certain regions. We'll clarify in the cost doc.

[15:50] James O'Neill: Timeline recap — pilot start: 2026-06-08, run 3 weeks, evaluation by 2026-06-29, then decision on dedicated capacity. Are those dates ok?
[16:02] Sara Mitchell: Yes that works for our team.

[16:10] Diego Alvarez: Next steps: i'll schedule a 60min technical deep dive to go through VPC, terraform, and API rate limit tuning. I'll propose 2026-05-26 or 05-27.
[16:22] Maya Chen: Ravi will set up weekly 30-minute syncs beginning 2026-06-01 to track progress.

[16:30] Anika Rao: For the security review i'm going to send a questionnaire, please respond with SOC2 artifacts and KMS docs.
[16:38] Maya Chen: We'll respond by 2026-05-24 per the action items.

[16:46] [20:00] -- Slight crosstalk where someone drops in with a question about model catalog --
[20:08] Sara Mitchell: Do you support a curated model catalog? we have some internal fine-tuned models as well.
[20:16] Diego Alvarez: Yes we have a model catalog and can host customer-trained model artifacts in private deployments; we'll talk about versioning and rollouts in the technical deep dive.

[20:32] James O'Neill: We'll need a plan for model rollouts and canary tests; can Redwood do automatic fallbacks?
[20:38] Diego Alvarez: Yes automated fallback policies are supported, you can define route policies and fallbacks to cheaper variants.

[20:46] [30:00] -- Wrap up and recap --
[30:08] Maya Chen: Quick recap: Maya to send onboarding checklist and sandbox creds, Diego to send VPC terraform and schedule deep dive, Ravi to set up check-ins, Sara to share prompts and targets, Anika to send security questionnaire. We'll also send SOC2 and security pack.
[30:28] Sara Mitchell: That list looks good. Thank you.
[30:32] Ravi Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and calendar invites.
[30:36] Diego Alvarez: Thanks, looking forward to working with Lumina.
[30:40] [56:00] End meeting

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings (links and certain product names); refer to attachments for authoritative docs.
